overview:
### CI-published live badges replace hand-measured README numbers — Difficulty: 3/5

This change stops the README from going stale by replacing hard-coded measurements (test counts, catch rate, false-ask rate) with shields.io endpoint badges that CI regenerates on every push to `main`. The `Test & Coverage` job now tees the `bun test` output to a log, keeping the exit status through `pipefail`. A new `Publish badges` step reads pass/fail counts from that log, builds the CC hook adapter, runs `bench/hook-corpus.ts`, writes three shields JSON files, and force-pushes them as a single orphan commit to a `badges` branch. The README now shows the badges at the top and again under Numbers. The Numbers table lists how to measure each value instead of giving the value, and the prose that quoted fixed counts now points to the badges.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["push / pull_request"] --> B["Run tests: bun test --coverage | tee test.log"]
  B --> C{"always() and push to refs/heads/main?"}
  C -->|"no"| Z["skip publish"]
  C -->|"yes"| D["grep pass / fail counts from test.log"]
  D --> E{"fail != 0 or pass == 0?"}
  E -->|"yes"| F["tests.json color=red"]
  E -->|"no"| G["tests.json color=brightgreen"]
  F --> H["bun run build:hk-cc, then bun bench/hook-corpus.ts"]
  G --> H
  H --> I["grep 'caught X/Y, false asks A/B' and write catch.json + falseasks.json"]
  I --> J["git init -b badges, commit, push -f with GITHUB_TOKEN"]
  J --> K["README shields endpoint badges read raw badges/*.json"]
  class B,C,D,E,H,I,J,K chg
  classDef chg fill:#d6ffd9,stroke:#1a7f37,color:#111
  class J risk
  classDef risk fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc1111,color:#111
```

**Riskiest area:** the whole `test` job now has `contents: write`, including on same-repo pull requests where it runs code from the PR branch. The publish step also force-pushes with the token in the remote URL, and it parses the bench and test output with `grep`, so a format change in that output makes it publish empty or `0` badge values without failing.

## Strict review

Inline comments mark required changes. Requesting changes until every thread is resolved.

<!-- cc-review:review fnv1a32:85d0cc22 -->

comments.body:
Move the `Publish badges` step into a separate job with `needs: test` and scope `permissions: contents: write` to that job alone: the current placement grants write access to the repository for every step in the `test` job — including checkout, dependency install, build, and the test run itself — violating the principle of least privilege; GitHub Actions does not support step-level permissions, so the only correct fix is job-level isolation.

<!-- cc-review:finding 3b0436f0 -->
